subject: Tiered latency ladder & onramp for renewal (CloudFolio)
messages:
From: Elena Ramos <elena@cloudfolio.com>
To: markus_klein@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-11-01T09:14:00-07:00
Subject: Renewal: premium SLA + capacity onramp

Markus —

Thanks again for the demo last week. CloudFolio is planning to expand the usage surface for our conversational assistant in Q1 and we want the renewal to reflect a higher reliability bar and predictable throughput. Specifically, we'd like to discuss: 

- A premium SLA that includes a tiered latency ladder tied to committed throughput (example ask below).
- A three-month onramp plan to double peak QPS, with a hard cutover window in January.
- Clear crediting for missed latency SLOs and a short path for burst capacity.

Initial latency targets we're interested in (open to your guidance):
- Tier A (baseline commit): p95 < 250ms, p99 < 700ms
- Tier B (50% higher commit): p95 < 200ms, p99 < 600ms

If you can share a draft MAP and a rough commercial outline (price delta vs. our current renewal), that would be great. We're aiming to finalize terms by mid-November to allow procurement to run paperwork.

Thanks — happy to hop on a quick call if it's easier.

— Elena
Elena Ramos
Head of Platform Ops, CloudFolio

Elena —

Really appreciate the clarity. High level response and next steps below. I'll put a short mutual action plan together and loop in pricing/legal once we align on the technical bar.

Quick answers: 
- We can offer a tiered latency ladder tied to a committed throughput band. The latency bands you suggest look reasonable; we'll propose concrete numbers tied to committed sustained QPS and the percent of traffic subject to the SLO (e.g., 80% of requests measured at the API edge).
- For missed SLOs we propose a credit model (token-cost credits) plus an optional operational runway: an allowance of 2 burst-days per quarter before automatic burst capacity kicks in.
- Onramp: recommend a 4-week pilot (shallow burst), then a 6-week capacity ramp to reach sustained target. Cutover window in January is feasible.

I'll attach a draft amendment and a short performance appendix for your review. Can we schedule a 30-min technical sync with Camila and Aditya tomorrow (Nov 2) at 8:30am PT?

Proposed mutual action plan (high level):
- Week of Nov 6: Technical sync & finalize measurement definitions (owner: Camila).
- Nov 10: Pricing & commercial terms (owner: Markus).
- Nov 15: Legal/DocuSign draft ready (owner: Legal).
- Nov 20: Sign and start pilot (owner: CloudFolio ops).

Attachments: draft amendment (CloudFolio_SLA_Amendment_v1.pdf), performance appendix (Performance_Appendix.xlsx).

If that timeline works for you, I'll book the tech call.

— Markus Klein

Subject: Re: Renewal: premium SLA + capacity onramp — technical sync notes

Elena / team —

Quick technical notes following the sync today. I've captured assumptions we need to lock before we finalize SLO measurement and the pilot plan: 

1) Workload profile
- Typical sequence length: 40–120 tokens (avg 68).
- Top-heavy burst patterns during business hours (peak 2–3x baseline for ~90 minutes).

2) Measurement definition (we propose):
- Latency measured at the Redwood API edge (time from request arrival to first token flush + tail token) — reported p50/p95/p99 on server-side instrumentation.
- SLO applies to user-facing generation calls (not embeddings or background batch jobs).
- Exemptions: planned maintenance windows and known upstream datastore incidents.

3) Onramp & Pilot
- 30-day pilot (shared telemetry). During pilot we'll run two experiments: (A) baseline at current commit; (B) stress window at +50% sustained QPS for 48 hours to validate tail behavior.
- If we see p99 degradation >250% vs baseline during stress, we recommend a pause-and-tune with a small config change (quantization profile / batch sizing / KV cache sizing).

4) Operational requirements
- We need a single contact for on-call rotations during the ramp and a shared Slack channel (we'll provision).
- KMS key handing: if CloudFolio requires customer-managed keys for payload encryption, that will affect the onboarding lead time by ~2–3 weeks.

I'll include these items in the formal performance appendix. If any of this is incorrect, flag it in reply and we'll update the draft.

— Camila Reyes
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
camila_reyes@redwood.ai

Subject: Re: Renewal: premium SLA + capacity onramp — commercial approval

Markus / team —

I've reviewed the proposed ladder and the pilot plan. From a commercial standpoint we are willing to: 

- Approve a premium SLA with a two-tier latency ladder as long as the SLO measurement definitions match Camila's note.
- Offer a one-year pricing addendum with a 20% uplift on list for Tier A -> Tier B escalation (applied as a blended discount across year 1 consumption).
- Include two weeks of complimentary priority on-call training during the pilot period.

Conditions: CloudFolio must commit to a minimum 12-month term and provide a single technical point of contact with admin rights to enable telemetry. Legal will prepare an amendment to reflect the crediting model described by Markus.

Happy to sign off if CloudFolio confirms the 12-month term and the on-call contact.

— Hannah Schmitt
